full_name: Randomized stochastic AGD (RSAGD) algorithm for stochastic smooth optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Algorithm 6.4 and Theorem 6.12)

problem.description: The stochastic smooth problem considered in Section 6.4.2.1, with \(\Psi\) differentiable, bounded from below, and having Lipschitz continuous gradients.

assumptions.name: Convexity_and_solution
assumptions.math: \Psi(\cdot) \text{ is convex and an optimal solution } x^* \text{ exists for problem (6.4.1)}

steps.name: Randomized termination
steps.math: \text{If } k=R, \text{ terminate the algorithm. Otherwise, set } k=k+1 \text{ and go to step 1.}

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Let } \{x_k,\bar{x}_k\}_{k\ge1} \text{ be computed by Algorithm 6.4 and } \Gamma_k \text{ be defined in (6.4.11). Also suppose that Assumption 16 holds. (a) If } \{\alpha_k\}, \{\beta_k\}, \{\lambda_k\}, \text{ and } \{p_k\} \text{ are chosen such that (6.4.12) holds and } p_k=\frac{\lambda_kC_k}{\sum_{\tau=1}^{N}\lambda_\tau C_\tau}, \; k=1,\ldots,N, \text{ where } C_k \text{ is defined in (6.4.12), then for any } N\ge1, \text{ we have } \mathbb{E}[\|\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_R)\|^2]\le \frac{1}{\sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_kC_k}\left\{\Psi(x_0)-\Psi^*+\frac{L_\Psi\sigma^2}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_k^2\left(1+\frac{(\lambda_k-\beta_k)^2}{\alpha_k\Gamma_k\lambda_k^2}\sum_{\tau=k}^{N}\Gamma_\tau\right)\right\}, \text{ where the expectation is taken with respect to } R \text{ and } \xi_{[N]}:=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N). \text{ (b) Suppose that } \Psi(\cdot) \text{ is convex and that an optimal solution } x^* \text{ exists for problem (6.4.1). If } \{\alpha_k\}, \{\beta_k\}, \{\lambda_k\}, \text{ and } \{p_k\} \text{ are chosen such that (6.4.15) holds, } \alpha_k\lambda_k\le L_\Psi\beta_k^2, \; \beta_k<1/L_\Psi, \text{ and } p_k=\frac{\Gamma_k^{-1}\beta_k(1-L_\Psi\beta_k)}{\sum_{\tau=1}^{N}\Gamma_\tau^{-1}\beta_\tau(1-L_\Psi\beta_\tau)} \text{ for all } k=1,\ldots,N, \text{ then for any } N\ge1, \text{ we have } \mathbb{E}[\|\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_R)\|^2]\le \frac{(2\lambda_1)^{-1}\|x_0-x^*\|^2+L_\Psi\sigma^2\sum_{k=1}^{N}\Gamma_k^{-1}\beta_k^2}{\sum_{k=1}^{N}\Gamma_k^{-1}\beta_k(1-L_\Psi\beta_k)}, \quad \mathbb{E}[\Psi(\bar{x}_R)-\Psi(x^*)]\le \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{N}\beta_k(1-L_\Psi\beta_k)\left[(2\lambda_1)^{-1}\|x_0-x^*\|^2+L_\Psi\sigma^2\sum_{j=1}^{k}\Gamma_j^{-1}\beta_j^2\right]}{\sum_{k=1}^{N}\Gamma_k^{-1}\beta_k(1-L_\Psi\beta_k)}.
main_theorem.rate: The theorem gives parameter-dependent expected squared-gradient and convex function-gap bounds; the surrounding text specializes these to the SFO complexity rates stated around (6.4.6) and Corollary 6.16.
main_theorem.measure: expected squared gradient norm at the randomized search point, and in the convex case expected function gap at the randomized averaged point

proof.description: Define the stochastic gradient error and the search-point gradient difference used throughout part (a).
proof.produces: Definitions of \(\delta_k\) and \(\Delta_k\).

proof.description: Apply the smoothness upper model to the stochastic update, expand \(G(\underline{x}_k,\xi_k)=\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_k)+\delta_k\), and use Cauchy-Schwarz on the \(\Delta_k\) term.
proof.produces: First stochastic one-step descent inequality before bounding \(\Delta_k\).

proof.description: Use the deterministic gradient-difference bound (6.4.18) and then \(ab\le(a^2+b^2)/2\) to separate the gradient norm from the acceleration gap.
proof.produces: One-step descent with the acceleration gap \(\|\bar{x}_{k-1}-x_{k-1}\|^2\).

proof.description: Invoke the stochastic analogue of the deterministic acceleration-gap estimate (6.4.22). The PDF prints \(\delta_k\) in the first norm and then expands with \(\delta_\tau\) in the equality; this step preserves that display and uses the expanded line downstream.
proof.produces: Printed acceleration-gap display; the expanded equality gives the weighted sum of gradient, noise, and cross terms used in step 5.

proof.description: Substitute the acceleration-gap bound into the one-step descent and use \(\Gamma_{k-1}(1-\alpha_k)^2\le\Gamma_k\).
proof.produces: A one-step inequality ready to sum over \(k=1,\ldots,N\).

proof.description: Sum the one-step inequalities over \(k=1,\ldots,N\), keeping the double sum and stochastic cross terms explicit.
proof.produces: Summed inequality before reindexing the double sum.

proof.description: Reindex the double sum, use the definition of \(C_k\), and collect all inner-product noise terms into \(b_k\).
proof.produces: Summed descent inequality with coefficients \(C_k\) and martingale terms \(b_k\).

proof.description: Record the residual term used for martingale cancellation.
proof.produces: Definition of \(b_k\) and \(v_k\), with \(v_k\) depending only on \(\xi_{[k-1]}\).

proof.description: Take expectation with respect to \(\xi_{[N]}\); bounded variance controls \(\mathbb{E}\|\delta_k\|^2\), and the residuals vanish as martingale differences.
proof.produces: Expectation removes \(\sum_k b_k\) and bounds \(\mathbb{E}\|\delta_k\|^2\le\sigma^2\).

proof.description: Obtain the expected weighted gradient bound after the martingale cancellation.
proof.produces: Expected weighted sum inequality for part (a).

proof.description: Divide by \(\sum_k\lambda_kC_k\), use \(\Psi(x_N)\ge\Psi^*\), and use the part (a) randomization law to identify the randomized gradient expectation.
proof.produces: Theorem 6.12(a), equation (6.4.67).

proof.description: For part (b), apply the smoothness model to \(\bar{x}_k\), substitute the stochastic averaged update, and use convexity linearization at the search point.
proof.produces: Equation (6.4.72).

proof.description: Use the stochastic analogue of the Euclidean three-point identity, with the stochastic gradient in the update.
proof.produces: Three-point identity for the stochastic update.

proof.description: Expand the squared stochastic gradient norm into gradient, noise, and cross terms.
proof.produces: Expansion used to collect gradient, noise, and martingale terms.

proof.description: Combine (6.4.72), the stochastic three-point identity, and the norm expansion to isolate the deterministic gradient coefficient, the noise coefficient, and a residual inner product.
proof.produces: One-step convex-case stochastic inequality before applying Lemma 3.17.

proof.description: Subtract \(\Psi(x)\) from both sides of the one-step inequality and form the affine recursion to which Lemma 3.17 will be applied.
proof.produces: Derived recursion for \(D_k:=\Psi(\bar{x}_k)-\Psi(x)\): \(D_k\le(1-\alpha_k)D_{k-1}+B_k\), where \(B_k:=\frac{\alpha_k}{2\lambda_k}[\|x_{k-1}-x\|^2-\|x_k-x\|^2]-\beta_k\left(1-\frac{L_\Psi\beta_k}{2}-\frac{\alpha_k\lambda_k}{2\beta_k}\right)\|\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_k)\|^2+\frac{L_\Psi\beta_k^2+\alpha_k\lambda_k}{2}\|\delta_k\|^2+\left\langle\delta_k,(\beta_k+L_\Psi\beta_k^2+\alpha_k\lambda_k)\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_k)+\alpha_k(x-x_{k-1})\right\rangle\).

proof.description: Instantiate Lemma 3.17 with \(w_k=\alpha_k\), \(W_k=\Gamma_k\), the lemma's recursion sequence \(\delta_k\) instantiated as \(D_k\), and \(B_k\) equal to the explicit distance-difference, gradient, noise, and inner-product residual expression from previous_step:16.
proof.produces: The hypotheses of Lemma 3.17 hold with \(w_k=\alpha_k\) and \(W_k=\Gamma_k\): \(w_k\in(0,1]\) follows from Algorithm 6.4, while \(W_1=\Gamma_1=1\), \(W_k=(1-w_k)W_{k-1}\), and \(W_k>0\) are supplied by Gamma_weight_identity. Lemma 3.17 first yields \(D_N\le \Gamma_N(1-\alpha_1)D_0+\Gamma_N\sum_{k=1}^N B_k/\Gamma_k\). After dividing by \(\Gamma_N\), the derived weighted inequality before applying (6.4.30) is \(\frac{\Psi(\bar{x}_N)-\Psi(x)}{\Gamma_N}\le (1-\alpha_1)(\Psi(\bar{x}_0)-\Psi(x))+\sum_{k=1}^N\frac{\alpha_k}{2\lambda_k\Gamma_k}[\|x_{k-1}-x\|^2-\|x_k-x\|^2]-\sum_{k=1}^N\frac{\beta_k}{\Gamma_k}\left(1-\frac{L_\Psi\beta_k}{2}-\frac{\alpha_k\lambda_k}{2\beta_k}\right)\|\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_k)\|^2+\sum_{k=1}^N\frac{L_\Psi\beta_k^2+\alpha_k\lambda_k}{2\Gamma_k}\|\delta_k\|^2+\sum_{k=1}^N\Gamma_k^{-1}\left\langle\delta_k,(\beta_k+L_\Psi\beta_k^2+\alpha_k\lambda_k)\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_k)+\alpha_k(x-x_{k-1})\right\rangle\). The boundary term \(\Gamma_N(1-\alpha_1)D_0\) vanishes because \(\alpha_1=1\).

proof.description: Apply the deterministic distance telescope bound (6.4.30), using \(\alpha_1=\Gamma_1=1\), to replace the weighted distance-difference sum by \(\|x_0-x\|^2/(2\lambda_1)\).
proof.produces: Printed weighted recursion bound with residuals \(b'_k\).

proof.description: Record the convex-case residual term introduced by the preceding displayed inequality.
proof.produces: Definition of \(b'_k\) as a martingale-difference residual.

proof.description: Use the first relation in (6.4.68) to simplify the gradient coefficient and the noise coefficient.
proof.produces: Simplified convex-case deterministic/noise recursion.

proof.description: Take expectation with respect to \(\xi_{[N]}\), use bounded variance, and cancel \(b'_k\) by the same martingale argument as in part (a).
proof.produces: Equation (6.4.73).

proof.description: Fix \(x=x^*\) and use \(\Psi(\bar{x}_N)\ge\Psi(x^*)\) to bound the weighted sum of expected squared gradients.
proof.produces: Weighted gradient sum bound for part (b).

proof.description: Use the part (b) randomization law to convert the weighted sum bound into the randomized gradient bound.
proof.produces: Theorem 6.12(b) gradient bound, equation (6.4.70).

proof.description: Use (6.4.73) and \(\beta_k<1/L_\Psi\) to get the expected function-gap bound for any terminal index \(N\).
proof.produces: Terminal expected function-gap bound indexed by \(N\).

proof.description: Average the terminal function-gap bound over the randomized output distribution (6.4.69) to obtain (6.4.71).
proof.produces: Theorem 6.12(b) function-gap bound, equation (6.4.71).

key_lemmas.name: RSAGD_update_identities
key_lemmas.role: Provides the three update identities repeatedly substituted in the proof of Theorem 6.12.

proof.description: These identities are the printed update rules of Algorithm 6.4.
proof.produces: RSAGD update identities.

key_lemmas.name: Algorithm_6_4_alpha_domain
key_lemmas.role: Provides the Algorithm 6.4 input-domain facts used to justify \(\Gamma_{k-1}(1-\alpha_k)^2\le\Gamma_k\) and to remove the Lemma 3.17 boundary term.

proof.description: These are the printed input conditions on the acceleration weights in Algorithm 6.4.
proof.produces: \(\alpha_1=1\) and \(0<\alpha_k<1\) for \(k\ge2\).

key_lemmas.name: Gamma_weight_identity
key_lemmas.role: Normalizes the Jensen weights in the acceleration-gap estimate and supports the weighted telescoping arguments.

proof.description: Record the definition of \(\Gamma_k\) from (6.4.11) together with the Algorithm 6.4 input-domain facts for \(\alpha_k\). These give \(\Gamma_1=1\), \(\Gamma_k=(1-\alpha_k)\Gamma_{k-1}\) for \(k\ge2\), and \(\Gamma_k>0\) for the weight sequence used in Lemma 3.17 and Jensen's inequality.
proof.produces: \(\Gamma_1=1\), \(\Gamma_k=(1-\alpha_k)\Gamma_{k-1}\) for \(k\ge2\), \(\Gamma_k>0\), and the recurrence prerequisites for instantiating Lemma 3.17 with \(W_k=\Gamma_k\).

proof.description: Use the recurrence for \(\Gamma_k\) to rewrite \(\alpha_\tau/\Gamma_\tau\) as the difference of reciprocal weights, substitute \(\alpha_1=1\) and \(\Gamma_1=1\), and telescope.
proof.produces: The reciprocal weight identity (6.4.21), plus the derived normalized Jensen weights \(\Gamma_k\alpha_\tau/\Gamma_\tau\ge0\) whose sum over \(\tau=1,\ldots,k\) is one.

key_lemmas.name: Gradient_difference_bound
key_lemmas.role: Bounds the gradient-difference term in the part (a) one-step descent inequality.

proof.description: Apply Lipschitz continuity of the gradient to \((x_{k-1},\underline{x}_k)\), then use the search-point identity (6.4.8).
proof.produces: Equation (6.4.18).

key_lemmas.name: Proof_local_error_definitions
key_lemmas.role: Records the proof-local stochastic error and search-gradient difference definitions used in Theorem 6.12.

proof.description: The proof explicitly introduces these two notations before applying (6.4.7) and (6.4.64).
proof.produces: Definitions of \(\delta_k\) and \(\Delta_k\).

key_lemmas.name: Stochastic_acceleration_gap_bound
key_lemmas.ref: Proof of Theorem 6.12, lines 22138-22145; deterministic template Eq. (6.4.22)
key_lemmas.role: Controls the acceleration gap in part (a) after stochastic gradients replace exact gradients.

proof.description: Subtract the two stochastic update equations to get the stochastic analogue of the deterministic recursion printed at lines 21402-21403. The stochastic recursion is derived here from Algorithm 6.4 and the proof-local definition of \(\delta_k\), not printed in this deterministic template window.
proof.ref: Algorithm 6.4 and Eq. (6.4.22) deterministic template, lines 21400-21408
proof.produces: Derived stochastic acceleration-gap recursion: \(\bar{x}_k-x_k=(1-\alpha_k)(\bar{x}_{k-1}-x_{k-1})+(\lambda_k-\beta_k)(\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_k)+\delta_k)\).

proof.description: Divide the derived stochastic recursion by \(\Gamma_k\) and sum the resulting identity, following the deterministic transition printed immediately before (6.4.21).
proof.produces: Derived divided/summed stochastic identity: \(\bar{x}_k-x_k=\Gamma_k\sum_{\tau=1}^{k}\frac{\lambda_\tau-\beta_\tau}{\Gamma_\tau}(\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_\tau)+\delta_\tau)\).

proof.description: Apply Jensen's inequality to the divided/summed stochastic identity using the normalized weights from (6.4.21), following the deterministic proof of (6.4.22).
proof.produces: Derived Jensen stochastic analogue of (6.4.22): \(\|\bar{x}_k-x_k\|^2\le\Gamma_k\sum_{\tau=1}^{k}\frac{(\lambda_\tau-\beta_\tau)^2}{\Gamma_\tau\alpha_\tau}\|\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_\tau)+\delta_\tau\|^2\). The Jensen application uses \(\Gamma_k\alpha_\tau/\Gamma_\tau\ge0\) and \(\sum_{\tau=1}^k\Gamma_k\alpha_\tau/\Gamma_\tau=1\), supplied by Gamma_weight_identity from (6.4.21) and Algorithm 6.4's \(\alpha\)-domain.

proof.description: Record the two-line acceleration-gap display as printed in Theorem 6.12. The first line contains \(\delta_k\), while the equality line expands with \(\delta_\tau\); the expanded equality is the source expression used later.
proof.produces: Printed acceleration-gap display; downstream steps use the bracketed expanded equality.

key_lemmas.role: Converts convexity at the search point into the affine recursion used for Theorem 6.12(b).

proof.description: Split the difference into a convex combination and apply convexity at \(\underline{x}_k\).
proof.produces: Equation (6.4.26).

key_lemmas.ref: Proof of Theorem 6.12, lines 22215-22218; deterministic template Eq. (6.4.27)
key_lemmas.role: Turns the stochastic inner product in part (b) into a telescoping squared-distance difference plus a squared stochastic-gradient term.

proof.description: Expand \(\|x_k-x\|^2\) using \(x_k=x_{k-1}-\lambda_k(\nabla\Psi(\underline{x}_k)+\delta_k)\) and rearrange.
proof.produces: Stochastic analogue of (6.4.27).

key_lemmas.name: Squared_norm_expansion
key_lemmas.role: Separates deterministic gradient, stochastic noise, and martingale cross terms.

proof.description: Expand the square of a sum in the Euclidean norm.
proof.produces: Squared norm expansion.

key_lemmas.name: Distance_telescope_bound
key_lemmas.role: Controls the squared-distance terms after applying Lemma 3.17 in the convex part.

proof.description: Use the monotonicity condition (6.4.15) to telescope the weighted squared-distance differences and drop the final nonpositive term.
proof.produces: Equation (6.4.30). The final equality uses \(\alpha_1=1\) from Algorithm 6.4 and \(\Gamma_1=1\) from Gamma_weight_identity to rewrite \(\alpha_1\|x_0-x\|^2/(\lambda_1\Gamma_1)\) as \(\|x_0-x\|^2/\lambda_1\).

key_lemmas.name: Lemma_3_17
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let } w_k\in(0,1], \; k=1,2,\ldots, \text{ be given. Also let } W_k:=\begin{cases}1, & k=1,\\ (1-w_k)W_{k-1}, & k\ge2.\end{cases} \text{ Suppose that } W_k>0 \text{ for all } k\ge2 \text{ and } \delta_k\le(1-w_k)\delta_{k-1}+B_k, \; k=1,2,\ldots. \text{ Then, we have } \delta_k\le W_k(1-w_1)\delta_0+W_k\sum_{i=1}^{k}(B_i/W_i).
key_lemmas.role: Provides the weighted recursion/telescoping tool used to pass from the one-step convex recursion to the \(\Gamma_N\)-weighted inequality.

proof.description: Divide the base inequality and the later inequalities by \(W_k\).
proof.produces: Scaled recursive inequalities.

proof.description: Sum the scaled inequalities and rearrange the telescoping terms.
proof.produces: \(\delta_k\le W_k(1-w_1)\delta_0+W_k\sum_{i=1}^{k}B_i/W_i\).

key_lemmas.name: Martingale_difference_cancellation
key_lemmas.role: Cancels the residual inner-product sums in both parts of Theorem 6.12 after taking expectation.

proof.description: The proof notes that \(v_k\) only depends on \(\xi_{[k-1]}\), so it is measurable before the oracle noise \(\delta_k\) is sampled.
proof.produces: \(v_k\) is \(\xi_{[k-1]}\)-measurable.

proof.description: Use Assumption 16(a) to make the conditional mean of \(\delta_k\) vanish, hence the conditional mean of the residual inner product is zero.
proof.produces: \(\{b_k\}\) is a martingale-difference sequence; the same reasoning applies to \(\{b'_k\}\).
